'''''Ambrosia psilostachya''''' is a species of [[Ambrosia (plant)|ragweed]] known by the common names '''Cuman ragweed''' and '''perennial ragweed''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''western ragweed'''.

==Distribution and habitat==
The plant is widespread across much of [[North America]] ([[United States]], [[Canada]], and northern [[Mexico]]).<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Ambrosia%20psilostachya.png Biota of North America Program 2104 county distribution map]</ref> It is also naturalized in parts of [[Europe]], [[Asia]], [[Australia]], and [[South America]].<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=AMPS United States Department of Agriculture Plants Profile] . accessed 2.14.2013</ref> It is a common plant in many habitat types, including disturbed areas such as roadsides.<ref name=z>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242416043 Flora of North America Vol. 21 Page 18 ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' de Candolle in A. P. de Candolle and A. L. P. P. de Candolle]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242416043 Flora of China Vol. 20-21 Page 877  <big>裸穗豚草</big> luo sui tun cao  ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' Candolle]</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/2701652?tab=specimens Tropicos, specimen listing for ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' DC]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=ambrosia+psilostachya Altervista Flora Italiana, Ambrosia con spighe rade, ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' DC.] includes photos and European distribution map</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:562128 Atlas of Living Australia, ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' DC. Perennial Ragweed]</ref>

==Description==
''Ambrosia psilostachya'' is an erect perennial herb growing a slender, branching, straw-colored stem to a maximum height near two meters, but more often remaining under one meter tall. Leaves are up to 12 centimeters long and vary in shape from lance-shaped to nearly oval, and they are divided into many narrow, pointed lobes. The stem and leaves are hairy.<ref name=z/>

The top of the stem is occupied by an [[inflorescence]] which is usually a spike. The species is [[plant sexuality|monoecious]], and the inflorescence is composed of [[Stamen|staminate]] (male) flower heads with the [[gynoecium|pistillate]] heads located below and in the axils of leaves.<ref name=z/> This bloom period is from June through November.

The pistillate heads yield fruits which are [[achene]]s located within oval-shaped greenish-brown [[Burr (fruit)|burs]] about half a centimeter long. The burs are hairy and sometimes spiny. The plant reproduces by seed and by sprouting up from a creeping [[rhizome|rhizome-like]] root system.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Robert L. |last1=Neill |first2=Elroy L. |last2=Rice |date=October 1971 |title=Possible Role of ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' on Pattern and Succession in Old-Fields |journal=American Midland Naturalist |volume=86 |issue=2 |pages=344–57 |jstor=2423628 |doi=10.2307/2423628}}</ref>

==Ecology==
''Ambrosia psilostachya'' is a host plant for the caterpillars of ''[[Bucculatrix transversata]]'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=American Entomological Society |url=http://archive.org/details/memoirsofameric181963amer |title=Memoirs of the American Entomological Society |date=1916 |publisher=Philadelphia, American Entomological Society |others=Smithsonian Libraries}}</ref> ''[[Cosmopterix opulenta]]'', ''[[Exaeretia gracilis]]'', ''[[Gnorimoschema saphirinella]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ambrosia |url=http://www.nic.funet.fi/pub/sci/bio/life/plants/magnoliophyta/magnoliophytina/magnoliopsida/asteraceae/ambrosia/#psilostachya |access-date=2022-04-09 |website=www.nic.funet.fi}}</ref> ''[[Schinia sexplagiata]]''; the beetles ''[[Calligrapha disrupta]]'', ''[[Calligrapha suturalis]]'';<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Clark |first1=S. M. |last2=LeDoux |first2=D. G. |last3=Seeno |first3=T. S. |last4=Riley |first4=E. G. |last5=Gilbert |first5=A. J. |last6=Sullivan |first6=J. M. |date=2005-03-01 |title=Host plants of leaf beetle species occurring in the United States and Canada (Coleoptera: Megalopodidae, Orsodacnidae, Chrysomelidae, excluding Bruchinae) |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1603/0013-8746(2005)098[0243:hpolbs]2.0.co;2 |journal=Annals of the Entomological Society of America |volume=98 |issue=2 |pages=243–244 |doi=10.1603/0013-8746(2005)098[0243:hpolbs]2.0.co;2 |issn=0013-8746|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and the grasshopper ''[[Spharagemon collare]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pfadt |first=Robert |title=Spharagemon collare |url=http://idtools.org/id/grasshoppers/factsheet.php?name=13216 |access-date=2022-04-08 |website=Grasshoppers of the Western U.S.}}</ref>

==Medicinal uses==
This plant had a number of medicinal uses among several different [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] tribes, including the [[Cheyenne]], [[Kumeyaay people|Kumeyaay (Diegueno)]], and  [[Kiowa people]].<ref>[http://herb.umd.umich.edu/herb/search.pl?searchstring=Ambrosia+psilostachya  University of Michigan at Dearborn: Native American Ethnobotany of ''Ambrosia psilostachya''] . accessed 2.14.2013</ref>

==Chemistry==
''Ambrosia psilostachya'' contains a group of [[phytochemical]]s called [[psilostachyin]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wan |first1=Shiqiang |last2=Yuan |first2=Tong |last3=Bowdish |first3=Sarah |last4=Wallace |first4=Linda |last5=Russell |first5=Scott D. |last6=Luo |first6=Yiqi |s2cid=14548075 |year=2002 |title=Response of an allergenic species, ''Ambrosia psilostachya'' (Asteraceae), to experimental warming and clipping: Implications for public health |journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=89 |issue=11 |pages=1843–6 |pmid=21665612 |doi=10.3732/ajb.89.11.1843 |bibcode=2002AmJB...89.1843W }}</ref>
